status: Compatibility patch; final full-scene GPU playback unverified
changes: Program variants depend only on uniforms declared by that material, not every shared scene uniform.
Water-field sampling flags are initialized before startup shader preparation.
Fine-particle lighting uses shared illumination caches and bounded water absorption, with opaque-depth clipping.
Compatible hardware uses the pre-existing single-resolution GPU water field; NVIDIA RTX keeps nested fields.
Disabled rain is not speculatively compiled or drawn by the live renderer.

gpuTesting.pipeline: Full default beach physics, 13,293 water samples, wind 24, 96 by 64 image, one completed frame at a time
gpuTesting.outcome: Earlier nested-field candidates reproduced compiler failures when loose sand appeared at 0.6 simulated seconds. A later candidate with dynamic geometry counts lost its context during its first paused frame. Testing was stopped; that broader specialization change was reverted. No application or machine restart was performed.
gpuTesting.interpretation: Do not treat passing CPU checks or a build as proof the reported full-scene crash is resolved.

preExistingTestFailure.test: tests/sand-drops-rigid.test.js: sand/object constraints cannot submit GPU work, including deferred and packed modes
preExistingTestFailure.detail: Backend label assertion expects CPU object contacts but receives JavaScript CPU.

tradeoffs: The compatible GPU path reconstructs the original full water field, so it gives up the new nested-field texture savings.
Fine particles retain spectral water scattering but use approximate cached lighting instead of individual geometry-shadow rays.
